questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

At the academic competition, the five first-place winners from different schools were recognized for their outstanding achievements and presented with scholarships to further their education.
o: At the academic competition, the five first-place winners
and presented with scholarships to further their education
from different schools were recognized for their outstanding achievements
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'At the academic competition, the five first-place winners'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'At the academic competition, the first five-place winners' should be used instead of 'At the academic competition, the five first-place winners'.
  • In the given sentence 'five and first' are the numeral adjectives.
  • They are arranged in a particular order which is as follows: Ordinal (first) + Cardinal (three).
    • Example: The first → (Ordinal) five → (Cardinal) students will receive the Chief Guest. 
       

Correct Sentence: At the academic competition, the first five-place winners from different schools were recognized for their outstanding achievements and presented with scholarships to further their education.

questions.q: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
o: The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
questions.s:
Answer: 3
Solution: The correct sentence is: "The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo."
The word "tallest" is the correct superlative form of "tall".
We do not use “most” or “more” with adjectives that already form their superlative/comparative by adding –er or –est.

Why other options are incorrect:
Option 1 – "more taller" ❌: double comparative (more + taller) is grammatically incorrect.
Option 2 – "most taller" ❌: mixing superlative "most" with comparative "taller" is wrong.
Option 4 – "most tallest" ❌: "tallest" is already a superlative; adding “most” creates a redundancy.

Difficult Word Meaning:
Superlative – the highest degree of comparison (सर्वश्रेष्ठ रूप)
Tallest – the most tall (सबसे लंबा)

questions.q:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He cheated in the [A] / examination, making his [B] / already-falling academic [C] / credentials worst. [D]
questions.s:
The error is in segment D, where "worst" should be "worse." "Worst" is the superlative form, used when comparing more than two items, while "worse" is the comparative form, appropriate here for comparing the current state to the previous one.

The correct sentence: He cheated in the examination, making his already-falling academic credentials worse.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.
